source_text: III. Igitur apprehensis nobis et apud [regionantes — sense unclear: local officials?] in custodia constitutis, sententiam praesidis milites nuntiare audivimus, quod heri corpus nostrum minaretur urere. nam, ut postea quoque verissime cognovimus, exurere nos vivos cogitavit. sed dominus, qui solus de incendio servos suos potest liberare, in cuius manu sermones et corda sunt regis, furentem a nobis saevitiam praesidis avertit. et incumbentes precibus assiduis tota fide statim quod petivimus accepimus: accensus paene in exitum nostrae carnis ignis extinctus est et flamma [caminorum — scan cammorum] ardentium dominico rore sopita est. nec difficile credentibus fuit nova posse ad vetera exempla pertingere, domino per spiritum pollicente quia qui gloriam istam operatus est in tribus pueris, vincebat et in nobis. IV. Tunc a proposito suo domino repugnante confractus, mitti nos in carcerem iussit. quo deducti a militibus sumus, nec expavimus foedam loci illius caliginem; moxque carcer tenebrosus spiritu perlucente resplenduit, et contra obscuritatis deformia et caeca nocte contecta instar diei fidei devotio candida luce nos vestiit. et ad summum ascendebamus locum poenarum quasi ascenderemus in caelum. quales illic dies duximus, quales transegimus noctes, exponi nullis sermonibus possunt; tormenta carceris nulla affirmatione capiuntur, nec veremur atrocitatem loci illius ut est dicere. quo enim temptatio grandis est, eo maior est ille qui eam vincit in nobis. et non est pugna, quia est domino protegente victoria. nam et occidi servis dei leve est, et ideo mors nihil est, cuius aculeos comminuens contentionemque devincens dominus per trophaeum crucis triumphavit. sed et nulla causa armorum est nisi quando miles armandus est, nec armatur nisi quando congressio est; et in coronis nostris ideo praemium est quia certamen ante praecessit, nec datur palma nisi congressione perfecta. sed paucis diebus visitatione fratrum refrigeravimus; nam omnem noctis laborem diei solatium laetitiaque abstulit.
thought_title: Fire Quenched and Dark Prison Made Bright
orientation: The imprisoned confessors writing together report how the plan to burn them alive was turned aside and how their dark prison became bright.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore when we had been seized and had been set in custody among regionantes, we heard soldiers announce the decision of the governor, that yesterday he was threatening to burn our body. For, as afterwards also we learned most truly, he had planned to burn us alive. But the Lord, who alone is able to free his servants from fire, in whose hand are the words and hearts of the king, turned away from us the raging cruelty of the governor. And pressing upon unceasing prayers with whole faith, immediately what we asked we received: the fire kindled almost to the destruction of our flesh was extinguished, and the flame of the burning furnaces was quenched by the dew of the Lord. Nor was it hard for believers that new things can reach to old examples, with the Lord promising through the Spirit that he who worked this glory in the three boys was conquering also in us. Then broken from his purpose with the Lord resisting him, he ordered us to be sent into prison. To which we were led down by soldiers, and we did not dread the foul darkness of that place; and soon the dark prison shone bright with the Spirit shining through it, and against the deformities of darkness and things covered by blind night the devotion of faith as day clothed us with white light. And we were going up to the highest place of punishments as if we were going up into heaven. What sort of days we led there, what sort of nights we passed through, can be set forth by no words; the torments of prison are grasped by no assertion, and we do not shrink from speaking the harshness of that place as it is. For where temptation is great, there greater is he who conquers it in us. And there is no battle, because with the Lord protecting there is victory. For also to be killed is light for servants of God, and therefore death is nothing, whose stings crushing and whose contest defeating the Lord triumphed through the trophy of the cross. But also there is no cause for arms except when the soldier must be armed, nor is he armed except when there is a meeting in combat; and in our crowns for this reason there is reward because struggle went before, nor is the palm given except with the meeting in combat completed. But in a few days by the visit of the brothers we were refreshed; for all labor of night the comfort and joy of day took away.

put to sleep, quenched of flame here
reach to, extend to old examples here
trophy, victory sign of cross here

choices.why: cogitavit plus vivos makes the threat a live burning, matching the brief argument
scan reads cammorum, sense requires furnace fire quenched by dew like the three boys
fixed glossary for the whole trial as contest before reward
fixed glossary for martyr vindication and reward
literal rore keeps the cooling liquid image against fire, not a polished quenching

pass_b_english: Once we had been seized and placed in custody under guard, we heard soldiers announce the governor's sentence, that yesterday he threatened to burn our bodies. For as we later learned with complete certainty, he had meant to burn us alive. But the Lord, who alone can rescue his servants from the fire (Daniel 3), in whose hand are the words and the hearts of the king, turned the governor's raging cruelty away from us. We gave ourselves to constant prayer with total faith, and we received at once what we asked: the fire kindled almost to destroy our flesh was extinguished, and the flame of the burning furnaces was lulled to sleep by the dew of the Lord. To believers it was not hard to trust that new wonders could reach back to the ancient examples, since the Lord promises through the Spirit that he who worked this wonder in the three young men would win his victory in us too.

Then, broken as the Lord stood against his purpose, he ordered us to be sent to prison. Soldiers led us there, and we did not fear the foul darkness of that place. Soon the dark prison shone bright as the Spirit shone through it, and against the ugliness of the gloom and the blind night wrapped around us, faithful devotion clothed us in white light like day. We were climbing to the highest place of punishment as if we were climbing into heaven. What days we spent there, what nights we endured, no words can describe. No account can capture the torments of prison, yet we do not hesitate to call that place cruel as it truly is. For where trial is great, greater still is he who conquers it in us. There is no battle, because with the Lord protecting us there is victory. Even to be killed is a light thing for the servants of God, and so death is nothing, for the Lord crushed its stings and defeated its assault and triumphed through the trophy of the cross. There is also no call for arms except when a soldier must be armed, and he is armed only when an encounter comes. So too our crowns hold reward because struggle came first, and no palm is given unless the encounter is fought to the end. After a few days we were refreshed by a visit from the brothers, for the comfort and joy of daytime took away every hardship of the night.
notes: regionantes is flagged in source as sense unclear, glossed only as set in custody among regionantes without deciding the office
caminorum is supplied for scan cammorum, glossed as furnaces with uncertainty noted
